prompt:
Below is a plan for a software change. Decide, for each reference problem, whether the plan addresses the same underlying problem anywhere in its text (names it as a risk, or plans for it specifically), even if worded differently.

Change request: Make ky retry POST and PATCH requests by default when the network fails, so that flaky mobile connections stop failing.

Reference problems:
1. Adding post and patch to defaultRetryOptions.methods in source/utils/normalize.ts would cause Ky to retry on retry.statusCodes (such as 500, 502, 503, and 504) as well as network failures, violating the request to only retry when the network fails. This would re-execute failed server-side mutations for HTTP error responses that should have failed immediately.
2. Because POST and PATCH are non-idempotent methods, retrying on a NetworkError introduces duplicate server-side side effects if the connection was interrupted after the server received and processed the initial mutation. Ky has no way of discerning whether a network failure occurred before the request reached the server or after the server began handling it.
3. In source/core/Ky.ts, connection drops produce a NetworkError whereas request timeouts throw a TimeoutError, which is governed separately by retry.retryOnTimeout (defaulting to false). Flaky mobile connections frequently fail via timeouts, meaning the change would either fail to resolve mobile drops or, if retryOnTimeout is broadened, unsafely retry requests that the server is still actively executing.
4. In source/core/Ky.ts, #fetch() calls this.request.clone() whenever retry.limit > 0, which invokes ReadableStream#tee() on streaming bodies. Enabling retries for POST and PATCH by default will force every streaming upload to buffer unconsumed chunks in memory, risking excessive memory consumption or out-of-memory crashes on resource-constrained mobile devices.
5. If a POST or PATCH request body is a ReadableStream that was disturbed or locked during an interrupted initial attempt, Request.clone() in #fetch() will throw an unhandled TypeError on the retry attempt rather than recovering cleanly. This would cause flaky mobile requests to crash with native stream errors rather than surfacing a clean NetworkError.
6. When using onUploadProgress, streamRequest in source/utils/body.ts pipes the request body through a progress-tracking transform stream. Retrying an interrupted POST or PATCH upload will cause progress events to restart from 0%, triggering confusing progress regressions or duplicate completion events in client UIs.
7. Existing custom retry.shouldRetry hooks that return undefined rely on Ky falling through to default method checks that reject POST and PATCH. Enabling POST and PATCH retries by default would alter this fallback behavior, silently triggering retries for existing applications that expect undefined to reject non-idempotent requests.
8. This change directly breaks existing test assertions in test/retry.ts—specifically tests like 'not on POST' and 'NetworkError is not retried for non-retriable method (POST)'—which enforce that POST requests fail fast without retrying. Changing this default represents a breaking change in Ky's core HTTP semantics for existing consumers.
9. POST and PATCH mutations frequently carry headers such as Idempotency-Key or authorization nonces generated for a single attempt. Retrying automatically without re-running beforeRequest hooks or providing a mechanism to refresh request-specific tokens will cause backends to reject retried requests as duplicate or invalid submissions.
10. Compatibility with existing retry config – Projects may already specify a custom retry object that omits methods. Overriding the default could unintentionally extend the retry set, breaking assumptions in tests or CI pipelines.
11. Network‑error detection – Ky decides whether an error is “network” via isNetworkError. Certain mobile edge cases (e.g., DNS‑lookup failures) may be classified differently, causing inconsistent retry behavior for POST/PATCH versus GET.
12. Server‑side rate limiting – Automatic retries on POST/PATCH may repeatedly hit rate‑limit responses (429) and ignore afterStatusCodes handling, leading to rapid back‑off loops and possible bans.

Plan:
I've written and [term] the plan (Phases 0a–6). No repo file was edited; the only file written is the plan at `claude-home/plans/standard-make-ky-retry-drifting-feigenbaum.md`.

## What the code shows
- The default retry methods (`source/utils/normalize.ts:17`) don't include `post` or `patch`.
- The method check in `#calculateRetryDelay` (`source/core/Ky.ts:703`) gates every reason to retry: status codes, timeouts and network errors alike. So just adding `post`/`patch` to `retry.methods` would also retry POST on 500/502/503/504/429. The server certainly received those requests, so retrying them is the wrong fix.
- Retrying won't cost extra memory. Ky already copies the request body (`Ky.ts:1225`) for POST whenever `limit > 0`.
- The project's own docs already say the core risk out loud (`readme.md:581`): "a network error does not tell whether the server got the request."

## Assumptions (no one to ask in this run)
- **A1:** "Network fails" means a `NetworkError` while the request is being sent (`Ky.ts:1268`). It excludes HTTP status errors, timeouts, and a connection that drops while the response body is being read (`Ky.ts:905`), where the response has already arrived.
- **A2:** `retry.methods` stays unchanged.
- **A3:** This changes default behaviour, so it ships as 3.0.0 with a migration note.
- **A4:** The project keeps no lessons file; AGENTS.md (no `null` anywhere) is the only rule that applies.

## Plan
- **New option:** `retry.networkErrorMethods`, default `['post', 'patch']`.
  - For a method only in this list, any error that isn't a network error is rethrown *before* `shouldRetry` runs, so POST behaviour on HTTP errors and timeouts doesn't change.
  - On a network error, `shouldRetry` can still veto by returning `false`.
  - Retries forced with `ky.retry()` work as today.
  - Opting out is `[]`. Passing `null` throws "retry.networkErrorMethods must be an array" through the existing check.
- **Deliverables:**
  - **D01:** types and their docs in `source/types/retry.ts`.
  - **D02:** default value and validation in `normalize.ts`.
  - **D03:** split the method check in `Ky.ts`.
  - **D04:** tests and type tests.
  - **D05:** readme, migration note, and an Idempotency-Key example.
- **Verify:** `npm test`, plus the browser tests in CI.

**Independent [term] (one round): APPROVE.** I folded in its five fixes:
- **`.extend()` can't opt out:** it merges retry arrays by joining them (I checked `merge.ts:353`), so a child's `networkErrorMethods: []` doesn't clear a list the parent set. Only `replaceOption([])` does. This gets documented and tested.
- **Docs that need rewording:** they say `shouldRetry` runs "after method checks pass" (`types/retry.ts:143`, `readme.md:281`, `readme.md:304`).
- **Types:** add a mutable field to `MutableRetryOptions` and update the strict type test in `test-d/normalized-options.ts`.
- **Copying:** copy the array during normalization so hooks can't change it for other requests.
- **Extra test:** POST + `shouldRetry: () => true` + a 500 response must still send exactly one request.

## Main risks

| # | Risk | Why it bites here | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Side effects run twice (double charge or double create) | A network error doesn't prove the server didn't commit: undici's `terminated`, `Network connection lost` and Safari's `Load failed` can all happen after the server processed the request | Loud docs, an Idempotency-Key example, `shouldRetry` as a veto; accepted on purpose |
| 2 | POST also retried on 5xx/429 | The method check gates every reason to retry (`Ky.ts:703`) | Separate option; tests that 5xx/429 POST isn't retried |
| 3 | Existing users' behaviour changes silently | New default in a library on 2.2.0 | 3.0.0 plus a migration note |
| 4 | `.extend()` can't turn it off | Retry arrays are joined when merged (`merge.ts:353`) | Document `replaceOption([])`; test it |
| 5 | `null` config quietly accepted | AGENTS.md forbids `null` | The existing array check throws; add a test |
| 6 | `shouldRetry: true` brings back retries on HTTP errors | Today `shouldRetry` overrides the default checks | Rethrow non-network errors before `shouldRetry`; test it |
| 7 | Streamed uploads fail again on every retry | Chromium sends streamed bodies only over HTTP/2+; upload progress restarts at 0 | Docs; the existing `beforeRetry` `{options}` escape hatch |
| 8 | Retry storm against a server that's recovering | Many mobile clients reconnect at the same time | Existing backoff and `limit: 2`; recommend jitter |
| 9 | Type definitions drift | `NormalizedRetryOptions` is derived from `MutableRetryOptions` | Update the strict type test |
| 10 | Docs contradict the code | Several places say "after method checks pass" | Reword all four places |

Riskiest: #1. A retried POST/PATCH after a network failure can run a non-idempotent write twice, and no code-level check can rule that out.
